executiveSummary: GM1916 is identity-correct and passes the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract, but its first-72-hour results are not calibrated to Leidschendam-Voorburg. The major-river preset holds legacy flood amplitude 0.835583 through T+72, affecting 19,475 people-equivalent, and coastal reaches 1.909012 and 41,977 affected at T+24 without selecting a sea/Rhine boundary condition, primary or regional defence failure, Vliet/Delfland/Rijnland boezem pathway, connected footprint, arrival or recession. Official evidence instead shows a municipality spanning two water boards, very low pumped polders, over four metres of local managed-level difference, a Vliet-east dike section that does not meet safety requirements, and urban pluvial sensitivity from hard surface and small floor-to-road separation. Eight unrelated hazards reuse exactly the same top neighbourhood order; compound keeps identical flood amplitude, pressure, affected count and critical status from T+24 to T+72. All services reuse eight road-derived border links even though public context includes 54 water assets, Stedin/Dunea planning, 102 antenna registrations, HMC Antoniushove without an emergency department, one ProRail station and 80 transit stops. Suppress unsupported flood and lifeline precision; retain current NoData, the official scoped zero of no municipal emergency support points, and modeled zeros distinctly; and require authority-confirmed water, route, hospital and action state before altering recovery.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — Official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, safety-region and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS 2025; BAG/BRT deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS inputs identify GM1916 as Leidschendam-Voorburg in Zuid-Holland and report 78,318 residents, density 2,402/km², 23.5% aged 65 or older and 15,804 one-person households.

The reference point [4.4141270873302885, 52.08832993601589] lies inside the 2025 generalized polygon. All 43 neighbourhoods and thirteen districts load; neighbourhood population sums to 78,310, eight below the municipal total because small-area values are rounded or suppressed.

BAG supplies two woonplaatsen, Leidschendam and Voorburg, under Public Domain Mark 1.0. BRT TOP10NL under CC BY 4.0 additionally labels Stompwijk, Park Leeuwenbergh and Wilsveen, for five settlement features in total. No BAG centre lies outside the generalized boundary.

CBS/BAG/BRT do not measure commuters, patients, visitors, Vlietland recreation, event crowds, home-care dependency, evacuation need, household emergency stocks or incident-time presence. Generalized geometry cannot resolve polders, dikes, peilgebieden, sewers, tunnels, buildings or nature fuels.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Water and sewer programme 2022–2027 and local climate-adaptation evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal water and sewer programme 2022–2027; current webpages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The programme says urban water nuisance occurs earlier because of extensive hard surface and can cause greater damage because dense homes, shops and businesses have small differences between floor and road elevation. It says earlier polder storage deficits were largely addressed but climate change continues.

The current municipality page treats heavy-rain water nuisance together with drought and heat adaptation across Leidschendam, Stompwijk and Voorburg: https://www.lv.nl/slim-omgaan-met-te-veel-of-te-weinig-water. It does not publish a live event footprint or complete machine susceptibility layer.

The programme distinguishes wastewater, rainwater, groundwater, municipal sewer duties and water-board responsibilities. Its assets, measures and policy targets are planning/design evidence, not current capacity, maintenance condition, blockage, pump operation or spare capacity.

The municipal document and pages have document-specific dates but no blanket machine reuse licence or guaranteed refresh cadence identified. They cannot validate the model's exact depth, ranking, affected count or restoration curve.

evidenceSources.publisher: Hoogheemraadschap van Delfland / Hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Dual-water-board polder, boezem, dike and public asset context
evidenceSources.edition: Joint agenda announced 17 June 2026; HWH deployment snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Delfland, Rijnland and the municipality signed a 46-project agenda through 2030 for water storage, robust water systems, dike improvement, water quality, drought and heat. This proves two water-board systems and active adaptation, not an incident-time state.

Delfland's 21 July 2026 Tedingerbroekpolder page describes three nearby managed levels: about -1.90 m NAP in the high polder, -4.80 m NAP in low Leidschenveen and -0.43 m NAP in the Delfland boezem, a difference exceeding four metres: https://www.hhdelfland.nl/actueel/nieuwsoverzicht/2026/juli/vernieuwd-gemaal-tedingerbroekpolder/. These are system/design references, not flood depth.

Rijnland says the approximately four-kilometre dike along the Vliet/Rijn-Schiekanaal east of Leidschendam protects the land behind it but no longer meets safety requirements; design and field investigations were active in 2026: https://www.rijnland.net/over-rijnland/wat-doet-rijnland/in-uw-buurt/dijkverbetering-de-vliet-oostzijde-leidschendam/. Project status is not failure probability or current breach.

The GM1916 HWH intersection contains 54 points: 29 surface-water pumps, thirteen weirs, ten sluices and two sewer pumps. HWH IMWA is weekly CC BY-SA 4.0; DAMO is contributor-dependent CC BY-SA 4.0: https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2 and https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1

Delfland describes the Vliet in Voorburg as part of its boezem at -0.43 m NAP and says its control room may pre-pump ahead of forecast rain: https://www.hhdelfland.nl/ontdek-werk/juiste-waterpeil/waterpeil-regelen/. Points and plans do not establish connected catchments, compatible capacity, current operation, power/backup, defence state, water quality or recovery.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel Veiligheidsregio Haaglanden 2023
supports: Haaglanden's profile identifies low terrain and shallow groundwater, potential large Randstad flooding from sea or rivers, heavy rain/cluster showers, wind, heat, drought, power/gas/telecom outage, cyber and cross-regional dependencies.

The profile says dense population, ageing, commuters, students and visitors increase consequence and describes motorways, rail, waterways, pipelines and tunnels. A small traffic incident can cause regional gridlock.

Nature-fire risk is regionally limited compared with dune areas but longer dry and hot periods increase it. This supports scenario inclusion while requiring local fuel/source evidence rather than a uniform regional multiplier.

The document is strategic regional planning, not a GM1916 flood footprint, event probability, real-time warning, incident population, service percentage, resource assignment or restoration schedule. No blanket open-data licence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Official flood-scenario, weather and Waterinfo evidence routes
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO release 2025.1.6; weather/water deployment snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: LIWO is an official WMCN flood-scenario library exposed through https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows. IPLO says correct interpretation requires specialist water-manager knowledge. Releases are irregular and individual-layer licence/metadata must be checked.

A governed sea/Randstad or Rhine scenario must retain release/scenario, source water body and boundary hydrograph/datum, primary and regional defence state, breach/overtopping mode, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability/context, resolution, coverage, licence, NoData and expert approval. LIWO is not observed flooding.

No KNMI station, RWS Waterinfo observation or Waterinfo forecast point is assigned inside GM1916 in the deployment snapshots. KNMI ten-minute observations are CC BY 4.0 and Waterinfo generally ten-minute CC0 public guidance: https://dataplatform.knmi.nl/dataset/10-minute-in-situ-meteorological-observations-1-0 and https://www.rijkswaterstaat.nl/water/waterdata

Empty intersection is NoData/coverage, not zero rain, water level, discharge or hazard. Observations, forecasts, official hydraulic scenarios, strategic plans and synthetic checkpoints are different evidence classes and must never be silently fused.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Vlietland nature, recreation and dated nature-fire measures
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal notice dated 13 August 2026; current terrain pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: On 13 August 2026 the municipality reported exceptional prolonged drought, nature-fire phase 2 and a smoking, barbecue and open-fire ban at Vlietland. That is a dated operational measure and must not be projected to a different scenario valid time or interpreted as ignition.

Staatsbosbeheer describes Vlietland as a 300-hectare, year-round recreation area between the Vliet and A4 with water, forest, grass, beaches, watersport, camping and no bus stop; 60 hectares are managed by Staatsbosbeheer: https://www.staatsbosbeheer.nl/uit-in-de-natuur/locaties/vlietland/toegankelijkheid

A seasonal weekend rescue post is described for June–August. That published schedule is not proof it is open, staffed, reachable or equipped in an incident, and it is not a municipal emergency support point.

The public pages provide authoritative context with no blanket open-data licence identified. They do not supply ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture, spread, smoke concentration, visitor occupancy, suppression water or evacuation state.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / HTM / Nationaal Dataportaal Wegverkeer
evidenceSources.title: E07 — A4/A12/N14/N206, Sijtwendetunnel, rail and transit context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail/GTFS/NDW snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; current RWS tunnel page
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB geometry generates eight logical border edges: A4 north and south, A12 west, N14 west/north-west, N434 north, and N206 east/south-east. Repeated A4, N14 and N206 identities are single physical corridors/series edges, not additive independent capacity.

RWS says the five-kilometre N14 links A4 and N44 through three Sijtwendetunnels—Vliet, Park and Spoor—with 2x2 lanes and no emergency lane. Static tunnel facts and planned maintenance are not incident-time passability or evacuation throughput.

One ProRail station, Voorburg, lies inside GM1916; the static GTFS deployment contains 80 stop areas including HMC Antoniushove and RandstadRail/tram/bus stops. HTM notes the Leidschendam-Voorburg stop curve prevents all doors being accessible: https://www.htm.nl/reizen/toegankelijkheid/toegankelijkheid-van-halten/. Schedules and accessibility notes do not establish live operation.

No qualifying NDW record is assigned in the bounded snapshot published 2 September 2026 15:25 UTC. NDW DATEX is CC0 unless stated otherwise; an empty intersection means no matching message, never that every motorway, tunnel, Vliet bridge, rail or transit service is open.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Leidschendam-Voorburg / HMC / RIVM / Stedin / Dunea / RDI / DUO / KVK-PDOK
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Current preparedness, health-care, utility, telecom and facility context
evidenceSources.edition: Current official pages inspected 3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026; deployment snapshots retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: The municipality currently states that Leidschendam-Voorburg has no emergency support points and is preparing locations; it directs residents to Denk Vooruit, NL-Alert, Haaglandenveilig and Omroep West. This is an authoritative scoped current zero, not proof of future absence, staffing, supplies or activation.

RIVM's CC0 2026 acute-care questionnaire assigns no emergency department inside GM1916. HMC confirms Antoniushove in Leidschendam has a GP out-of-hours post but no emergency department and directs 24/7 emergencies to HMC Westeinde in The Hague: https://www.haaglandenmc.nl/antoniushove/. This creates local hospital-continuity and cross-boundary acute-care dependencies, not guaranteed acceptance or access.

The one-point NBNL sample at postcode 2264KW maps to Stedin Noordsingel and reports 34.2 MW existing versus 41.5 MW required withdrawal, 4.2 MW queued across twelve requests, eleven projects and earliest project year 2026. At-least-quarterly/monthly planning with no exact dataset licence identified is not outage telemetry, current load, topology or restoration: https://data.partnersinenergie.nl/capaciteitskaart/totaal/afname

Stedin's December 2025 Noordsingel study describes congestion and planned expansion toward 2034: https://www.stedin.net/-/media/project/online/files/zakelijk/congestiemanagement/samenvatting-station-noordsingel---leidschendam-voorburg-en--den-haag-mariahoeve.pdf. Dunea's March 2026 page describes a future Vliet intake/pretreatment project for post-2030 regional supply: https://www.dunea.nl/algemeen/nieuws/2026/groen-licht-voor-dunea-in-de-leidschendammerhout. Neither is a current outage or emergency capacity result.

RDI WFS returns 102 antenna registrations—49 mobile, fourteen fixed-link, 36 radio-amateur, one broadcast and two other-mobile—with no fixed cadence or reuse licence stated. Daily DUO RIO under CC attribution returns 39 education records: 21 primary, seven secondary, one special and ten other. These do not establish coverage, backhaul, shelter, staffing, occupancy, stock or live state.

The KVK-PDOK partial Public Domain Mark 1.0 government-services subset and local PM2.5 layer return no assigned GM1916 point. These scoped no-matches are NoData/incomplete coverage, not absence of government functions or clean-air proof.

identity.summary: Official code, name, province, safety region, centre and headline demography agree.
notes: Feature id and regional bundle equal GM1916 / Leidschendam-Voorburg, assigned uniquely to Veiligheidsregio Haaglanden.
The centre lies within the 2025 generalized boundary and the official settlement assignment is coherent.
Annual inputs, 2022–2027/2023 policy, 2026 projects/observations and synthetic checkpoints retain separate dates and evidence classes.

geography.summary: The municipality geometry is coherent, but dual water boards, low polders, Vliet/boezem, tunnels and Vlietland require full-resolution causal geometry.
notes: Leidschendam, Voorburg and Stompwijk span dense urban land, low pumped polders, Vliet corridors and recreation/nature between A4 and the Vliet.
The Tedingerbroek/Leidschenveen/Delfland-boezem level references and Vliet-east dike project show that municipality-centre distance cannot establish hydraulic connectivity or depth.
Use full-resolution dike, peilgebied, AHN/BGT, sewer, water/land, tunnel/crossing and fuel geometry with explicit coverage/NoData before local exposure.

demography.summary: Official 2025 totals agree and neighbourhood rounding is explicitly reconciled.
notes: Population 78,318, density 2,402/km², age65Pct 23.5 and one-person households 15,804 agree with the generated municipality.

Neighbourhood population totals 78,310 (-8); the deterministic local allocation reconciles exactly to 78,318 across 43 rows. Published household rows total 37,715 and rounded age65+ rows total 18,425.
The older-resident share and dense population are planning context, not people needing evacuation, cooling, medicines, shelter or acute care.

regionalDetail.summary: All 43 neighbourhoods load, but several published fields, asset layers and every operational state are incomplete.
notes: Largest neighbourhoods are Prinsenhof hoog 4,705, Voorburg Oud noord 4,295, Bovenveen midden 4,160, Voorburg Noord zuid 3,760 and Voorburg Noord noord 3,205.
District heat and charging are missing for 43/43 neighbourhoods; twelve other CBS measures are missing for one row. Null or suppressed values remain Unknown, never zero.
HWH provides 54 partial points but no complete sewer/boezem topology or state; NBNL, RDI, DUO and KVK are context with their own sampling/coverage limits.

settlements.summary: Two BAG places and five BRT settlements are retained, but Stompwijk/rural and recreation-area occupancy/access remain unknown.
notes: Leidschendam and Voorburg are the two BAG woonplaatsen; BRT additionally represents Stompwijk, Park Leeuwenbergh and Wilsveen under cartographic settlement types.
Do not duplicate the municipal population across labels or infer a measured visitor/resident count from a named core.
Incident-time commuters, Vlietland visitors and water/tunnel/crossing isolation are Unknown.

transport.summary: A4/A12/N14/N434/N206, one station and 80 stops load, but eight border edges omit internal tunnels, Vliet crossings and live access.
notes: A4, N14 and N206 each appear on multiple boundary relations sharing one physical corridor; their nominal 260/150-unit logical ceilings are not additive measured throughput.
The N14 includes three separate tunnels without an emergency lane. The model lacks tunnel, Vliet bridge, critical junction, rail/RandstadRail/bus and destination-state semantics.
NWB is valid only for mobility and eligible logistics/repair access, never physical utility topology. Empty NDW is not all-open, and HMC Westeinde acceptance/travel remains Unknown.

emergencyContext.summary: Regional risks and current preparedness guidance are authoritative, but no action/resource state supports 0–72-hour decisions.
notes: The municipality's current statement of zero emergency support points is a verified narrow fact; future sites, readiness, staffing, stock, opening and capacity remain Unknown.
HMC Antoniushove is a critical local hospital facility but has no SEH; 24/7 emergency care at HMC Westeinde is cross-boundary and not guaranteed available or reachable.

Required action classes include warning, dike/boezem/polder/pump/sewer control, evacuation/welfare, road/tunnel/bridge/rail/transit control, hospital continuity/transfer, Vlietland fire/smoke, temporary water, reception, food/fuel/medicine, utility repair and mutual aid.
No incident-time warning, asset operation, route state, hospital acceptance, staff, generator/fuel, stock, crew or confirmed action is ingested; preparedness guidance is not recovery evidence.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets produce finite deterministic results at every required checkpoint and service; causal realism failures are separate.
notes: The focused gate covered severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

At T+72 river still reports amplitude/severity 0.835583/0.264833, pressure 0.316501, 19,475 affected and 1,733,284 person-hours. Compound still reports amplitude 0.482485, pressure 0.546385, 44,842 affected and critical status, with severity 0.478960 and 3,067,106 person-hours. These are synthetic exercise indices, not observations, casualties or outages.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact zero-event behavior, reconciliation and cumulative-burden contracts pass.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1916 pnpm audit:model passed one file and two tests in 29.70 seconds, with 29.48 seconds test execution; the final current-code rerun also passed in 29.43 seconds, with 29.21 seconds test execution.
Intensity-zero runs are exact zero, repeats and UI/core presets agree, selected service does not change local physical hazard, and route flow stays within logical ceilings.
All 78,318 residents and 43 neighbourhoods reconcile in every local map; demand, delivery and causal ledgers close and event-attributable person-hours are monotonic against the matched baseline.
Arithmetic consistency does not establish local calibration or turn absent evidence into safety.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Unsupported river/coastal amplitudes and one common neighbourhood ranking conflict with dual-boezem, polder, urban and Vlietland mechanisms.
notes: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire have the identical top order Duivenvoorde, Leidschendam-Zuid De Oude Bleijck, Bovenveen midden, Voorburg Noord noord, De Rietvink/Veursestraatweg, Voorburg West noord and Prinsenhof laag. Compound uses the same set with one swap.

The common order does not encode the dual water-board boundary, four-metre managed-level gradient, Vliet-east dike, urban floor/road vulnerability, population/heat vulnerability, Vlietland fuels/visitors or any cyber target.

River is persistent at amplitude 0.835583 through T+72 and coastal reaches 1.909012 at T+24 without a source reach/sea boundary, defence state, connected footprint, arrival or recession. Legacy floodDepthM must not be presented as surveyed metres.
Canonical wildfire has direct fire exactly zero, drought 0.678241 and smoke 0.288304 at T+24; the dated Vlietland phase-2 measure validates neither that scenario time nor the generic smoke field.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service percentages are inspectable but not calibrated to water boards, Stedin, Dunea, telecom, transport, hospitals or stocked supply.
notes: All eight services reuse eight NWB border edges because routes do not declare supportedServices; A4/N14/N206 duplicates are non-additive. Road geometry cannot represent electricity, drinking water, sewer/boezem, gas, telecom, hospital or inventory connectivity.

At compound T+24 modeled availability is power 0.312829, water 0.351222, drainage 0.322747, gas 0.571353, telecom 0.267623, mobility 0.814546, facilities 0.346873 and supply 0.813550. No cited operator or authority validates these exact values.

HWH assets, NBNL planning, Stedin congestion, future Dunea intake, RDI points, hospital/education records and transit stops remain context; none provides current switching, pressure/quality, pump state, backhaul, stock, staffing, backup or restoration.
Sensitive/unavailable topology must remain Unknown or use a clearly documented aggregate synthetic dependency graph with uncertainty ranges.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic closes, but hydraulic source, common spatial allocation, cyber/fire targets and physical-network provenance do not.
notes: Service-stage deltas, weighted pressure, local demand/delivery and matched-no-event person-hour arithmetic reconcile.

River/coastal derived screens omit selected water body, boundary hydrograph/datum, primary/regional defence or breach/overtopping state, boezem/polder connectivity, footprint, arrival/duration/recession and expert approval.
Wildfire lacks ignition/perimeter/fuels/plume and cyber lacks a named target/architecture/attack path; earthquake lacks a selected KNMI event, site-response field and asset fragility.
Current official no-support-point status, 2026 projects/fire measure, empty deployment feeds, 2023 strategic risks and synthetic scenario state remain distinct evidence classes.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent flood and compound trajectories lack local water-control, access, hospital, utility, stock and action evidence.
notes: River amplitude/severity is exactly unchanged from T+24 through T+72 while affected people increase and pressure worsens; no source hydrograph, dike state, pumping, recession or repair input supports the plateau.

Compound amplitude, pressure, affected count and all eight service availabilities remain exactly at their T+24 values through T+72, while cumulative person-hours rise to 3,067,106. No authority action or operator restoration plan supports that exact persistence.

Coastal direct amplitude returns to zero by T+72 but 10,164 affected remain; heat severity remains nonzero while affected rounds to zero. Current zero, residual modeled consequence and unresolved evidence must be displayed separately.

No warning, water-control action, tunnel/bridge/rail reopening, hospital acceptance, utility crew, temporary water, support point, reception, food/fuel/medicine or household stock is ingested. Seventy-two hours is a preparedness horizon, not a restoration deadline.

findings.summary: The major-river preset fabricates persistent precise local flooding without a selected Rhine/Vliet/boezem pathway.
findings.evidence: River reports legacy amplitude 0.835583 and severity 0.264833 at both T+24 and T+72, with affected people-equivalent increasing from 17,241 to 19,475 and cumulative person-hours reaching 1,733,284. E03–E05 identify dual boezem/polder systems and possible Randstad river flooding, but no source reach, hydrograph, defence state or connected footprint supports this result.
findings.action: Suppress direct river severity, affected population and attributable service effects in GM1916 until WMCN, Delfland, Rijnland and VRH select a versioned connected scenario. Preserve indirect regional-network disruption separately and keep unresolved Vliet/boezem/polder paths Unknown, never zero/safe.

findings.summary: The coastal preset creates catastrophic local impact without a sea boundary, defence failure or Randstad footprint.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 reports legacy amplitude 1.909012, severity 0.596748, pressure 0.520430, 41,977 affected and 878,534 person-hours. The municipality is inland but can be affected through Randstad primary-defence scenarios; E04/E05 do not validate a direct coastline-distance scalar, uniform depth or exact service cascade.
findings.action: Keep the diagnostic screen internal and expose direct local output as unsupported/Unknown until a named LIWO sea/Randstad scenario supplies boundary hydrograph/datum, defence/breach/overtopping state, connected footprint, arrival/recession, true units, probability/context, version, licence, coverage/NoData and expert approval.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated hazards reuse one full local ordering that contradicts known water, urban, heat and nature mechanisms.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share the exact T+24 top sequence led by Duivenvoorde and Leidschendam-Zuid De Oude Bleijck. Compound uses the same top seven with one swap. E02/E03 distinguish hard-surfaced urban water nuisance, low polders/boezems and dike conditions; E06 identifies Vlietland; cyber has no target.
findings.action: Retire the shared neighbourhood seed. Require hazard-specific versioned surfaces/targets and explicit NoData or render distribution Unknown. Add regressions for dual-boezem flood connectivity, urban pluvial/heat, Vlietland wildfire/smoke, cyber target locality and exact service-layer hazard invariance.

findings.summary: Pluvial precision omits urban terrain, sewer, groundwater and dual-water-board control.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports amplitude 0.466567, 12,287 affected and 348,883 person-hours. E02 says hard surface and small floor-to-road separation make urban damage plausible; E03 shows multi-level pumped systems and 54 partial assets. No hyetograph, AHN/BGT, sewer-included flag, blockage/capacity, groundwater/saturation, pump state, model resolution or NoData supports the exact output.
findings.action: Integrate a governed municipality/Delfland/Rijnland stress-test or hydraulic result retaining rain event, terrain, imperviousness, sewer/overland assumptions, groundwater, pump/boezem boundary, edition, resolution, licence, uncertainty and NoData. Until then label local depth/ranking/count unsupported.

findings.summary: Vlietland wildfire and smoke are not spatially or temporally causal.
findings.evidence: At T+24 wildfire has direct fire zero, drought 0.678241, smoke 0.288304, severity 0.139050 and 502 affected while using the generic local order. E06's phase-2/open-fire ban is a real 13 August 2026 measure at Vlietland, but the preset has no aligned valid time, ignition/perimeter, fuels, wind/plume, visitors, access or suppression water.
findings.action: Require an explicit exercise or official ignition/perimeter, public/authorized fuel extent, time-aligned moisture/wind, spread/plume method, exposure unit, visitor state, access and suppression-water assumptions. A dated phase or static terrain page is context, not ignition probability or a T+72 forecast.

findings.summary: Road-derived service percentages overstate physical utility, water, telecom, hospital and supply knowledge.
findings.evidence: Eight NWB links feed every service and compound T+24 reports eight exact availability fractions from 0.267623 telecom to 0.814546 mobility. HWH, NBNL/Stedin, Dunea plans, RDI, hospitals and DUO provide no complete causal topology, present operating state, backup, switching, pressure/quality, backhaul, stock, staff, crews or restoration.
findings.action: Restrict NWB to mobility and eligible logistics/repair access. Use privacy/security-safe aggregate service zones and ranges or authorized operator aggregates; preserve publisher/version/time/licence/completeness/affectsSimulation. Unavailable topology/state stays Unknown or clearly aggregate synthetic.

findings.summary: N14 tunnel, Vliet crossings, transit and cross-boundary acute care are absent from first-72-hour reachability.
findings.evidence: The N14 contains three tunnels without an emergency lane; A4/N14/N206 duplicate edges share corridors; one ProRail station and 80 stop areas include Antoniushove, which has no SEH. HMC directs emergency patients to Westeinde in The Hague. Empty NDW and static schedules do not prove tunnel/bridge/rail/transit operation or hospital acceptance.
findings.action: Build internal multimodal reachability from NWB/BGT, tunnel/bridge data, ProRail, GTFS and waterway geometry, retaining ownership and static versus observed state. Add authorized HMC acceptance/diversion, critical utilities/supplies and transfer status. Missing operation/acceptance remains Unknown.

findings.summary: Water assets and infrastructure projects are valuable context but cannot calibrate event-time operation.
findings.evidence: HWH supplies 54 points and Delfland/Rijnland publish a renewed pump, dike improvement and 46-project agenda; Stedin and Dunea publish future capacity projects. These sources have different editions and semantics and do not establish current connectivity, comparable capacity, condition, defence reliability, outage or reserve.
findings.action: Retain registry/project facts as context-only with source collection, manager, nulls, edition, retrieval, licence and coverage. Seek authorized catchment/control and operator aggregates; never sum heterogeneous capacities or infer present safety/availability from project or point existence.

findings.summary: Local hospital presence can be misread as local 24/7 emergency-care availability.
findings.evidence: RIVM assigns zero SEH points inside GM1916 and HMC explicitly says Antoniushove has a GP post but no SEH; 24/7 SEH is at HMC Westeinde across the municipal boundary. Neither the empty acute layer nor hospital/transit labels establish no care need, live acceptance, beds, staffing, medicines, power/fuel or travel time.
findings.action: Represent Antoniushove's actual functions separately from SEH and model Westeinde/LUMC/Zoetermeer alternatives as time-dependent destinations. Ingest only authorized aggregate acceptance/diversion and continuity status; keep absent operational facts Unknown.

findings.summary: No auditable 0–72-hour action/resource ledger exists, and the municipality currently has zero emergency support points.
findings.evidence: E08 states that no emergency support points currently exist and locations are being prepared. The simulator nevertheless applies generic preparedness/intervention/recovery without confirmed warning, water control, evacuation, route control, hospital transfer, reception, distribution, crew or stock records. A planned support-point concept is not an open facility.
findings.action: Add Unknown-first proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled actions with responsible authority/operator, trigger, resources, source, issue/valid/expiry time, geography and confidence. Preserve the current official zero support-point count with retrieval time; only confirmed opening/staffing/stock may change response.

findings.summary: NoData, official zero and modeled zero need distinct semantics.
findings.evidence: No KNMI, Waterinfo, NDW, PM2.5, KVK or RIVM SEH point is assigned locally, and district heat/charging are null for every neighbourhood. Those are no-match/coverage or missing values, not safe weather/water/roads/air, no government or no care need. residualLimitations: This is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI, Rijkswaterstaat, WMCN, water-board, VRH or operator forecast, warning, probability estimate, evacuation order, casualty model or restoration promise.

No expert-selected sea/Randstad/Rhine/Vliet/Delfland/Rijnland event, boundary hydrograph, primary/regional defence or breach/overtopping state, connected footprint, arrival/recession, verified depth unit or NoData mask is ingested.

Generalized CBS and common neighbourhood geometry cannot resolve water/land, dikes, peilgebieden, terrain, hard surface, sewers, groundwater, buildings, tunnels, bridges, facilities, fuels, visitors or households.
CBS rows are rounded or suppressed; the -8 neighbourhood-population difference is publication semantics and null district-heat, charging and other fields remain Unknown.
Delfland and Rijnland plans/projects establish mechanisms and responsibilities but not current dike reliability, pump/sluice state, connected catchment, capacity, backup or recovery.
HWH point coverage is contributor-dependent; 54 registry objects do not form complete topology or prove compatible capacity, present operation, water quality or restoration.
LIWO 2025.1.6 requires scenario/layer selection, licence checking and specialist interpretation and is not an observed event.
No local KNMI, Waterinfo, NDW or PM2.5 point is assigned in the bounded deployment snapshots; absence is NoData/coverage rather than zero or safe state.
No complete safe-to-publish Stedin, Dunea, gas, telecom, sewer or water-control topology, live state, switching, backup, crews or restoration estimate is available in the model.
NBNL/Stedin congestion and Dunea's future Vliet project are capacity planning, not outage telemetry, household service or T+72 restoration evidence.
RDI registrations do not establish operator, coverage, backhaul, traffic, power/backup, damage, availability or restoration; no fixed cadence or reuse licence is stated.
NWB, RWS tunnel pages, ProRail and GTFS are static context and do not establish incident-time motorway, tunnel, bridge, rail, RandstadRail, tram, bus or waterway operation/throughput.
HMC Antoniushove is a hospital without SEH; HMC Westeinde's 24/7 role does not establish travel, acceptance, beds, staffing, medicines, oxygen, generator/fuel or incident capacity.
DUO and KVK do not establish command, shelter, support, reception, distribution, occupancy, staffing or capacity; zero KVK/SEH matches do not mean no government functions or care need.
The municipality currently reports zero emergency support points, but planned locations, dates, roles, capacity, staffing, stocks, accessibility and activation remain Unknown.
Vlietland phase 2 on 13 August 2026 is a dated measure; nature-fire risk changes with fuels, moisture, ignition, visitors, wind, spread/plume, access and suppression water.
Cyber lacks a named target, architecture, attack path and containment state; earthquake lacks a selected event, local ground motion/site response and asset fragility.
Preparedness, repair and intervention multipliers are exercise controls, not observed household readiness, authority decisions, resources or commitments.

Affected population is a people-equivalent exercise index and event-attributable person-hours is a matched-baseline weighted local service proxy, not casualties, patients, evacuations or customer outage-hours; six-hour checkpoints miss rapid change and 72 hours excludes prolonged recovery.
